CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
42-year-old female presents with right index finger pain sustained 5 days ago while skiing on double black diamond slopes. Patient lost control, fell, and jammed her index finger on an object during the fall. This was her only injury from the fall. Pain is rated 7/10. Patient has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. She has not iced the finger or applied a splint prior to this visit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation. Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand x-ray reviewed: normal, no fractures, all bones and joints in normal alignment. Physical examination of right index finger reveals tenderness to palpation over the distal interphalangeal joint, with pain on passive extension and flexion, and pain with direct compression over the joint.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: normal, no fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger. Plan: Apply splint to right index finger. Prescribe Mobic 15 mg once daily for 14 days for anti-inflammatory effect. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine if hand therapy is needed.
